newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Strong local demand aids Thai petrochemical growth.
newsitem.headline: Strong local demand aids Thai petrochemical growth.

text.p: Thailand is banking on strong and growing domestic demand to turn its petrochemical industry into a regional powerhouse, a senior industry official said on Monday.

Its 60 million people and predicted economic growth of seven percent or more until the end of the century provide a ready market for the industry's products, Kamolchai Pattaradom, president of National Petrochemical Plc (NPC) told a chemical industry meeting in Singapore.
"The strength of this domestic market thus allows establishment of world-scale plants in the country and enhancing export potential," Pattaradom said.
Thailand, a late entrant to the business, started up its first ethylene plant, the basic product used to make plastic products, in 1990.
The industry's output doubled to 700,000 tonnes per year in 1995 when a second plant began production. Now output is poised to surge to 3.0 million tonnes in the next three to four years.
Several new plants are planned to start before 2000, with the first by Thai Petrochemical Industry Plc due up early this year with an annual capacity of 350,000 tonnes per year.

Other companies planning to build at the same Mab Ta Phud site on the Gulf of Thailand are Siam Cement Plc for a 600,000-tonne plant due in 1999, a second plant by TPI, a third plant by NPC and one by a Bangkok Bank led group, Pattaradom said.
All the companies are also planing to build several plants that make use of the ethylene produced.
Pattaradom said Thailand was strategically situated in Indochina region and its combined population of around 230 million.
"The region still does not produce sufficient quantities of these products to meet the demand and significant import is needed from other regions," he said.
